name: Blake Baker
life: “I bought the keys and inherited eighteen decades of other people's expectations.” People around Breakwater Way know Blake by a small Monday habit. Blake stops on the landward side of the cycle track to watch the first boats turn for home.
voice: I'm the new owner. I promised a memorial special before I'd ever tasted what she ate.
appearance: Blake has short black hair swept back, a round face with a pronounced chin, and a favorite piece of clothing, a washed violet jersey. It usually goes with a pair of reading glasses in a cloth sleeve. When somebody else has the floor, Blake turns fully toward the person speaking.
personality: Blake takes a rejection personally for a day and analytically on the second morning. Blake can be generous with a rival once the first night's sleep has intervened.
agenda: To approve a memorial special only after tasting it.
family: Karina May is Blake’s cousin raised in the same household. Blake makes room at the table. Karina brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *Land without cranes*, Karina says, “I draw architectural renderings. I put a worker in mine and realized there'd be no job for the person I drew.”
connections: Lou Khan. A new deli owner learns who used to eat the other half. Also in the story is Freya King (menu adviser).

reactions.situation: The deli proposes serving the memorial sandwich every Sunday
reactions.response: Blake asks the family what they would want to eat on an ordinary Sunday.

reactions.situation: A frightened child is waiting outside a shuttered shop
reactions.response: Blake asks the nearest shop worker to stay too, then talks about ordinary things until the child can explain who is late.

reactions.response: Blake turns up the next morning with the one piece of advice that would have helped either of them.
